data.name: Grim Seventh
data.detailed_description:
Grim Seventh is a 3D Arcade Hack 'n' Slash game with a unique geometrical art style.

You are Agents! Mage-hunters sent by the human army to kill monsters and evil summoners with unknown motives. Agent, you are a mage yourself. You must defeat your enemies using all means necessary, being magic or steel. YOU MUST SURVIVE. As you will be rewarded if you complete your mission.

The Art

We chose an unique art style: Full 3D Geometrization. Using this style we gave those old, 2D hack'n'slash games a new turn.

The Music

The game's music is inspired on those power drums, epic tracks from Two Steps from Hell and other well known music groups.

Features

  • Fast-paced and dynamic combat
  • Smooth gameplay
  • Random level selection
  • Arcade elements (Scores, time attack, etc)
  • Professional, high quality, power EPIC music
  • Unique 3D geometrical art style

reviews.review:
Grim Seventh is a compact 3D hack-and-slash action game developed and published by Grimoire Games. Rather than attempting to deliver a sprawling role-playing adventure, it focuses on quick combat, arcade-style objectives, and replayable encounters. The player assumes the role of an Agent working as a mage-hunter for the human army, tasked with confronting monsters and mysterious summoners. There is an interesting irony in this premise because the Agent is also capable of using magic, creating the image of a warrior employing supernatural powers while hunting other practitioners of them. The story mainly serves as a foundation for the action rather than developing into an elaborate narrative.

Combat is the central attraction, combining magical abilities with conventional weapons. Grim Seventh is designed around fast encounters where positioning, attacking, and surviving are more important than managing complicated role-playing systems. Its top-down perspective complements this approach by providing a useful view of surrounding threats. The controls and overall structure aim for immediate accessibility, making it possible to understand the basic gameplay without spending a long time learning complex mechanics. This simplicity works well during short sessions, although players seeking a sophisticated combat system with extensive character builds and progression may eventually find the mechanics limited.

The arcade influence becomes particularly noticeable through scoring and time-based challenges. Instead of making progression the sole motivation, the game encourages players to improve their performance and tackle encounters more efficiently. Random level selection also introduces some unpredictability, helping prevent every session from following precisely the same sequence. These features provide a reason to return after becoming familiar with the fundamentals, especially for players who enjoy chasing better results. However, randomized content cannot completely compensate for a relatively modest amount of mechanical variety, so repetition can become increasingly apparent during longer sessions.

Visually, Grim Seventh distinguishes itself through its unusual geometrical 3D presentation. Its aesthetic attempts to reinterpret the feeling of traditional 2D hack-and-slash games within a fully three-dimensional environment. Characters, environments, and objects consequently have a deliberately angular and stylized appearance rather than striving for realism. This direction gives the game an identity that is easier to remember than a generic fantasy presentation would have been. At the same time, the minimalistic geometry can make some areas look sparse, meaning its appearance will probably appeal most to players who appreciate experimental indie visuals.

Music plays an important role in strengthening the atmosphere. The soundtrack takes inspiration from dramatic, percussion-heavy epic compositions, giving battles a larger sense of scale than the relatively simple visuals might otherwise suggest. This energetic musical approach suits a game centered on continuous combat, scoring, and survival. When the soundtrack, enemy encounters, movement, and attacks come together effectively, Grim Seventh can produce enjoyable bursts of intensity despite the modest scope of its underlying systems.

The biggest weakness is ultimately the limited depth supporting its appealing concept. The combination of magic, weapons, score chasing, timed objectives, and randomized levels establishes a functional arcade loop, but these elements do not develop into the kind of extensive progression expected from a larger action RPG. The narrative also remains secondary, leaving the potentially intriguing relationship between mage-hunters, summoners, monsters, and the magically capable protagonist largely unexplored. Players primarily interested in lore, character development, exploration, equipment collection, or intricate customization are therefore unlikely to find those qualities in substantial amounts.

Its focused design is not necessarily a disadvantage for everyone. Grim Seventh works better when considered an experimental arcade action title intended for brief sessions rather than a game meant to occupy dozens of hours. There is little unnecessary complexity between the player and the fighting, and the scoring structure provides additional motivation for anyone interested in mastering individual encounters. The modest technical presentation also reinforces the feeling of an independent project built around a specific gameplay idea instead of cinematic spectacle.

Grim Seventh is therefore a curious but uneven action game. Grimoire Games created something with recognizable personality through its geometrical art direction, energetic soundtrack, mixture of magic and steel, and emphasis on fast arcade combat. Its shortcomings emerge primarily from repetition, limited mechanical development, and a premise that could have supported considerably more narrative exploration. Players interested in obscure indie hack-and-slash games or score-driven action may discover some entertaining sessions here, while anyone expecting the depth of a substantial action RPG should approach it with more restrained expectations.

Rating: 6/10
